duncan-edwards.tagline: The Busby Babe many called the best of them all.
story: Born in Woodside, Dudley, in 1936, Edwards signed for United as a teenager and became the youngest player ever to play in the Football League First Division, and at the time the youngest England player since the Second World War. He played 177 matches for United and 18 times for England.

A left-half noted for his strength, toughness and authority on the pitch, he helped United win two league championships and two Charity Shields and reach the semi-finals of the European Cup, all in a professional career of less than five years. Many of his contemporaries described him as one of the best, if not the best, players they had played with.
He was one of the eight players who died because of the Munich air disaster. He survived the crash at first but died in hospital two weeks later, on 21 February 1958. He was 21.

bobby-charlton.tagline: A survivor of Munich, a World Cup winner and the captain of 1968.
story: Born in Ashington, Northumberland, Charlton made his United debut in 1956, aged 18, and soon had a regular place. He won the league in 1957, then survived the Munich air disaster in February 1958, rescued by his teammate Harry Gregg. He was the last survivor of the crash from the club.

He helped United win the FA Cup in 1963 and the league in 1965 and 1967, and captained the team that won the European Cup in 1968, scoring twice in the final as United became the first English club to win it. In 1966 he won the World Cup with England and was named European Footballer of the Year (the Ballon d’Or). He was known for his attacking instincts, his passing and his ferocious long-range shooting with either foot, and was cautioned only twice in his career.

His 758 matches and 249 goals for United stood as club records for many years: Ryan Giggs passed the appearances in the 2008 Champions League final. After leaving he managed Preston North End, and joined United’s board of directors in 1984. He died on 21 October 2023, aged 86.

denis-law.tagline: “The King” of the Stretford End and the only Scot to win the Ballon d’Or.
story: Born in Aberdeen in 1940, the youngest of seven children of a fisherman, Law began at Huddersfield Town. Manchester City then signed him for a British record fee, and Torino for another record. He found it hard to settle in Italy and signed for United in 1962 for £115,000, another British record.

He spent 11 years at United and scored 237 goals in 404 appearances, which places him third in the club’s history, behind Wayne Rooney and Bobby Charlton. Supporters called him “The King” and “The Lawman”, and opposing fans “Denis the Menace”. With Charlton and George Best he formed the “United Trinity”. He is the only Scottish player to win the Ballon d’Or, in 1964, and he holds the club record for 46 competitive goals in a single season.

He helped United win the FA Cup in 1963 and the league in 1965 and 1967, but missed the 1968 European Cup final through injury. He left in 1973 to return to Manchester City for a season, and played for Scotland at the 1974 World Cup. He died on 17 January 2025.

george-best.tagline: The genius who became football’s first celebrity.
story: Born in Belfast in 1946, Best was spotted at 15 by a United scout who sent manager Matt Busby a telegram: “I think I’ve found you a genius”. He made his debut at 17 and scored 179 goals in 470 appearances over 11 years, and was the club’s top league scorer for five seasons in a row.

A skilful dribbler with pace, balance and the ability to get past defenders, he was named European Footballer of the Year in 1968 and won two league titles, two Charity Shields and the European Cup with United. With his good looks and mop of dark hair he became one of the first celebrity footballers, and the Portuguese press called him “o Quinto Beatle” (the fifth Beatle) after a stand-out game in Lisbon in March 1966.

His lifestyle brought personal problems, above all alcoholism, which affected him on and off the pitch for the rest of his life. He won 37 caps for Northern Ireland but never played in a major tournament finals. He died on 25 November 2005, and was an inaugural inductee of the English Football Hall of Fame in 2002.

nobby-stiles.tagline: The tough-tackling “destroyer” who won the World Cup and the European Cup.
story: Stiles grew up in Collyhurst, in north Manchester, and supported United. After playing for England Schoolboys at 15 he got his childhood wish: an apprenticeship at the club in September 1959. He was an unlikely-looking footballer: short, with several teeth missing, very short-sighted and needing strong contact lenses. Matt Busby saw something in him anyway, and gave him his debut in October 1960 against Bolton Wanderers.
He spent eleven years at Old Trafford, renowned for his tough tackling and ball-winning, a “destroyer” in front of the defence. With United he won two league titles and the European Cup.

For England he won 28 caps and played every minute of the winning 1966 World Cup campaign, including the 4–2 final against West Germany. His post-match dance on the Wembley pitch, with the trophy in one hand and his false teeth in the other, was widely broadcast. He is one of only three Englishmen, with Bobby Charlton and Ian Callaghan, to have won both the World Cup and the European Cup. He died on 30 October 2020.

bryan-robson.tagline: “Captain Marvel”, the longest-serving captain in United’s history.
story: Born in Chester-le-Street, County Durham, and a Newcastle fan as a boy, Robson started at West Bromwich Albion, where he made over 200 appearances and was club captain, before moving to United in 1981. He became the longest-serving captain in the club’s history and was nicknamed “Captain Marvel”.

With United he won two league titles, three FA Cups and two Charity Shields, and the Cup Winners’ Cup in 1991. In August 2011 a poll of the club’s former players voted him the greatest ever United player.

He won 90 caps for England between 1980 and 1991, captaining his country 65 times (only Bobby Moore and Billy Wright have done it more often), and played at the 1982, 1986 and 1990 World Cups. After leaving United in 1994 he became player-manager of Middlesbrough, and he is now an ambassador for Manchester United.

mark-hughes.tagline: A fierce forward who went away and came back a bigger star.
story: Born in Ruabon, Wales, Hughes joined United after leaving school in the summer of 1980. He did not make his first-team debut for three years, scoring on it in a 1–1 League Cup draw at Oxford United in 1983–84. In 1984–85 he scored 25 goals in 55 matches as United beat Everton in the FA Cup final.

In 1986 he was sold to Barcelona for £2 million, and spent a season on loan at Bayern Munich. In May 1988 he returned to United under Alex Ferguson for what was then a club record fee of £1.8 million, and was a key player over the next seven years. He was the first player to win the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award twice, in 1989 and 1991, and is the only person to have scored in the Charity Shield, the League Cup final and the FA Cup final in the same season (1993–94).
For Wales he won 72 caps and scored 16 goals. He later managed Wales, Blackburn Rovers, Manchester City, Fulham, Queens Park Rangers, Stoke City, Southampton, Bradford City and Carlisle United.

peter-schmeichel.tagline: The giant Dane who captained United to the Treble.
story: Born in Gladsaxe, Copenhagen, Schmeichel spent eight seasons at United and won 15 trophies, including five Premier League titles and three FA Cups, and captained the club to victory in the 1999 Champions League final to complete the Treble. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers of all time: he was voted the IFFHS World’s Best Goalkeeper in 1992 and 1993, and was inducted into the English Football Hall of Fame in 2003.

A fierce competitor, he was tall and heavy enough to need specially made size XXXL shirts, and he often shouted at his defenders when he thought they had made a mistake. Unusually for a goalkeeper, he scored 11 goals in his career.

With Denmark he won the European Championship in 1992, and he was his country’s most capped player, with 129 games, until Simon Kjær overtook him in 2023. In a 2001 poll for Reuters the majority of 200,000 voters named him the best goalkeeper in history. His son Kasper is also a professional goalkeeper.

eric-cantona.tagline: “King Eric”: the number 7 who turned up his collar and turned United around.
story: Cantona played for Auxerre, Marseille, Bordeaux, Montpellier, Nîmes and Leeds United before ending his career at Manchester United, where he won four Premier League titles in five years, including two league and FA Cup Doubles. He wore the iconic number 7 shirt, was known for turning up his collar, and was nicknamed “King Eric” by United fans. A strong, technically skilful player with both creative and goalscoring ability, he was named by Pelé in the FIFA 100 list of the world’s greatest living players.

He was also outspoken and sometimes difficult: his time at United included a 1995 conviction for assaulting an abusive spectator, which brought a two-week prison sentence (reduced to community service on appeal) and an eight-month suspension from football. In 1997 he unexpectedly announced his retirement, just before his 31st birthday.

He then became an actor, appearing in films including Elizabeth and Looking for Eric. Inside United magazine voted him Manchester United’s greatest-ever player in 2003, and he was inducted into the Premier League Hall of Fame in 2021.

roy-keane.tagline: The captain who drove United through its most successful years.
story: Keane came from Cork, played for Cobh Ramblers and Nottingham Forest and then moved to United. During his 12 years at the club he won seven Premier League titles, four FA Cups and the Champions League, 17 trophies in all, and he captained the club from 1997 until he left in 2005. He was a dominating, box-to-box midfielder known for an aggressive and highly competitive style.

He is widely regarded as one of the greatest defensive midfielders of all time and one of the greatest players in Premier League history, and was named by Pelé in the FIFA 100 list. He was inducted into the Premier League Hall of Fame in 2021.

After United he joined Celtic and retired in 2006. He captained the Republic of Ireland for most of his 14 years as an international, though he was sent home from the 2002 World Cup after a dispute with the national coach over the team’s training facilities. As a manager he took Sunderland from 23rd in the Championship to the title and promotion, and later worked as a television pundit.

Neville joined United as an apprentice when he left school in 1991 and captained the youth side to FA Youth Cup glory in his first season. He made his senior debut on 16 September 1992, in a goalless home draw with Torpedo Moscow in the UEFA Cup. He was part of Alex Ferguson’s youth-oriented side of the 1990s, nicknamed “Fergie’s Fledglings” after the Busby Babes, with his brother Phil, Ryan Giggs, David Beckham, Nicky Butt and Paul Scholes.

In 1994–95 he became United’s first-choice right-back when Paul Parker was injured, and he stayed first choice until he retired. A right-back who spent his entire career at United, he captained the club for five years and won eight Premier League titles and two Champions Leagues. He was England’s first-choice right-back for more than ten years.
After retiring in 2011 he became a pundit for Sky Sports, was England’s assistant manager from 2012 to 2016 and briefly managed Valencia. He was inducted into the Premier League Hall of Fame in 2025.

paul-scholes.tagline: The midfielder other great players called the best of their generation.
story: Born in Salford in 1974, Scholes began training with United at 14 and joined as a trainee when he left school in 1991. He was one of Fergie’s Fledglings and made his full debut in 1994–95. He spent his whole professional career at United, scoring over 150 goals in more than 700 appearances, and made 718 appearances for the club, the third-highest total in its history.

He is renowned for his technical skill, accurate passing, intelligent movement and powerful shooting from long range. He won 25 trophies, including 11 Premier League titles (more than any other English player), three FA Cups and two Champions Leagues.

He retired in May 2011 and became a coach at the club, but returned to playing in January 2012 and played one more season before retiring for good in May 2013. For England he won 66 caps between 1997 and 2004, and retired from international football in August 2004, saying family life and his United career mattered more.

ryan-giggs.tagline: The most-capped, most-decorated player in United’s history.
story: Born in Cardiff, Giggs moved to Manchester at six when his father, the rugby league player Danny Wilson, joined Swinton. He began at Manchester City but joined United on his 14th birthday in 1987, made his debut in 1991 and spent the next 23 years in the first team. He retired at the end of 2013–14 with the club record of 963 competitive appearances.

He won 13 Premier League titles, more than any other player in history, as well as four FA Cups, two Champions Leagues and a long list of other honours. He was the first player to win the PFA Young Player of the Year award twice in a row, in 1992 and 1993, and the only player to play in each of the first 22 Premier League seasons and to score in each of the first 21.

Towards the end of 2013–14 he became United’s interim player-manager after David Moyes was sacked, then assistant manager under Louis van Gaal, and he left in July 2016. He won 64 caps for Wales, captained the Great Britain team at the 2012 Olympics, and was Wales manager from January 2018 until he resigned in June 2022.

david-beckham.tagline: The set-piece specialist who became a global icon.
story: Beckham made his first-team debut for United in 1992, aged 17. With United he won the Premier League six times, the FA Cup twice, the Charity Shield twice, the Intercontinental Cup and the Champions League in 1999. Primarily a right midfielder, he is considered one of the greatest set-piece specialists of all time, known for his passing and crossing.

He then played four seasons at Real Madrid, winning La Liga in his last, before joining LA Galaxy in 2007, with loan spells at AC Milan, and a short spell at Paris Saint-Germain. He retired in May 2013 after a 21-year career and is the only English player to have won a league title in four countries: England, France, Spain and the United States.

He made his England debut on 1 September 1996, captained his country for six years and won 115 caps in all. He was runner-up for the Ballon d’Or in 1999 and twice for FIFA World Player of the Year, and was inducted into the English Football Hall of Fame in 2008 and the Premier League Hall of Fame in 2021. He has been a UNICEF ambassador since 2005.

ole-gunnar-solskjaer.tagline: The “baby-faced assassin” who won the 1999 Champions League final.
story: Solskjær scored 115 goals in 109 league games for the Norwegian club Clausenengen and then moved to Molde, before joining United in July 1996 for £1.5 million. Nicknamed “the Baby-faced Assassin”, he made 366 appearances and scored 126 goals, and was renowned as a “super-sub” with a knack for scoring late goals off the bench.

His most famous goal came in injury time in the 1999 Champions League final: United trailed Bayern Munich 1–0 as the match entered stoppage time, and his winner secured the Treble. He stayed a regular until a serious knee injury in 2003 began to plague his career, and he retired in 2007.

He stayed at United as a coach and managed the reserve team from 2008, then led Molde to their first ever league titles. He returned to United in late 2018 as caretaker manager and was made permanent on 28 March 2019 after winning 14 of his first 19 matches. He took United to the 2021 Europa League final, lost to Villarreal on penalties, and was sacked in November 2021.

cristiano-ronaldo.tagline: From teenage winger to the world’s best player, twice over at Old Trafford.
story: After Sporting beat United 3–1 in a friendly on 6 August 2003, Alex Ferguson was determined to sign the young winger, calling him “one of the most exciting young players” he had ever seen. United signed Ronaldo on 12 August 2003 for £12 million, an England record for a teenager, and he was the first Portuguese player to sign for the club. He asked for the number 28 he had worn at Sporting but was given the number 7 shirt, previously worn by George Best, Eric Cantona and David Beckham.

He made his debut as a substitute in a 4–0 win over Bolton Wanderers on 16 August 2003. In his first spell he helped United win three consecutive Premier League titles, the 2007–08 Champions League and the 2008 FIFA Club World Cup, and for his performances in 2007–08 he won his first Ballon d’Or, at 23. In 2009 he joined Real Madrid for €94 million (£80 million), the most expensive transfer in history at the time.

He returned to United in 2021 and finished 2021–22 as the club’s top scorer with 24 goals. After a fall-out with manager Erik ten Hag, who used him as a substitute, United terminated his contract on 22 November 2022, following an interview in which he said he felt “betrayed”.

wayne-rooney.tagline: United’s all-time top goalscorer, and the scorer of that overhead kick.
story: After emerging as one of England’s top young talents at Everton, Rooney joined United in 2004 for £25.6 million. He was PFA Young Player of the Year in his debut season and PFA Fans’ Player of the Year in 2005–06, at 20. He was a key figure as United won three consecutive Premier League titles from 2006–07 to 2008–09 and reached three Champions League finals, in 2008, 2009 and 2011, winning the first. He also scored the winning goal in the 2008 Club World Cup final and was awarded the Golden Ball.

After his most prolific season to that point, 2009–10, he won the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award. He helped United reclaim the title in 2010–11 and won his fifth and final league title in 2012–13. In all he won 16 trophies with United, and he and Michael Carrick are the only two English players to have won the Premier League, FA Cup, Champions League, League Cup, Europa League and Club World Cup.

He is Manchester United’s all-time top goalscorer, with 253 goals. His February 2011 bicycle kick against Manchester City won the Premier League 20 Seasons Awards’ Best Goal award, and you can explore it in 3D below. He returned to Everton in 2017, later played for D.C. United and Derby County, and retired in January 2021. For England he is the youngest-ever goalscorer.

rio-ferdinand.tagline: The elegant centre-back and half of a famous defensive partnership.
story: Ferdinand began at West Ham United, made his Premier League debut in 1996 and became the youngest defender to play for England at the time. Leeds United paid a British record £18 million for him, and in July 2002 he joined United for around £30 million, breaking the British transfer record again. He won the Premier League in his first season, his first major club honour.

In September 2003 he missed a drugs test and was banned from football for eight months, from January to September 2004, which meant missing United’s FA Cup triumph and Euro 2004. When he came back he established himself and featured in the PFA Team of the Year four times in five years. He won another title in 2006–07 and a Premier League and Champions League double in 2007–08.

He won six Premier League titles and 14 trophies at United, and left when his contract expired in 2014. He played one season for Queens Park Rangers and announced his retirement on 30 May 2015. He won 81 caps for England and became a television pundit.

nemanja-vidic.tagline: The fearless Serbian captain who won the Premier League Player of the Season twice.
story: Vidić made his name at Red Star Belgrade, where he captained the club to a domestic double, and moved to Spartak Moscow in 2004. He joined United in January 2006 in a £7 million transfer and built a formidable defensive partnership with Rio Ferdinand.

In eight years at United he won five Premier League titles, three League Cups, five Community Shields, the Club World Cup and the Champions League. He is one of only five players to win the Premier League Player of the Season award twice, and the only defender ever to do so. He was made club captain in 2010 and held the armband for four years until he left.

In 2014 he joined Inter Milan on a free transfer and retired in January 2016 because of injury problems. For Serbia and Montenegro he was part of the “Famous Four” defence that conceded just one goal in the ten qualifying matches for the 2006 World Cup, a record for the fewest goals conceded.

edwin-van-der-sar.tagline: The goalkeeper who was still winning titles at 40.
story: Van der Sar was brought to Louis van Gaal’s attention at a relatively late age and made his name at Ajax, where he won the 1995 Champions League as the starting goalkeeper and was named Best European Goalkeeper. After Juventus and Fulham he joined United in 2005, and won the Champions League again in 2008, making him one of only eight players at the time to have won it with two clubs.

In 2008–09 he set a world record by not conceding a league goal for 1,311 minutes. In 2011 he became the oldest player to win the Premier League, at 40 years and 205 days. Among his individual awards are the Best European Goalkeeper award in 1995 and 2009 and UEFA Club Goalkeeper of the Year in 2009.

He retired as a professional in 2011, having won 26 major trophies in his career, mainly at Ajax and United, and 130 caps for the Netherlands, which made him his country’s most-capped player until 2017. He later became chief executive of Ajax.
